Maladaptive Strategies.value: I imagine getting revenge on the people responsible
constantly check body for signs of danger or injury
I detach myself from the memories

Threat.value: I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
I feel on guard even inside my own home

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.

Negative Appraisals.value: I acted in ways that go against who I am
Somebody else would have stopped the event from happening

vignette: Keenan is a 21-year-old African American chef who has been grappling with the aftermath of a sexual assault that occurred several months ago. Since the traumatic event, he has found himself constantly on guard and haunted by memories that intrude unexpectedly into his daily life. The assault happened late one evening after Keenan had closed up the restaurant where he worked. Walking home alone, he was confronted in an alleyway and violently attacked. The fear and helplessness he experienced during this assault are now manifesting through a range of symptoms, deeply impacting his life. One evening at work, the screeching tires outside the restaurant triggered a sudden sense of panic, sending Keenan into a state of hypervigilance. He immediately checked his surroundings for any signs of danger and began to monitor his body for any residual pain or injuries from the assault. This constant scanning for threats is something he does reflexively when triggered by sounds that remind him of the violence. Keenan often finds himself replaying the attack, but these memories are never straightforward. Something as simple as a car backfiring can instantly bring back the full memory of the incident without warning. When he tries to recount what happened, he loses his train of thought and feels unable to fully articulate his experience. During these moments, he hears echoes of voices from that night, adding to his distress. The trauma has left Keenan feeling violated not just physically but also in terms of his core values. He believes that he acted in ways that go against who he is, which exacerbates the memories and triggers. This belief that someone else would have prevented the assault adds to his sense of hopelessness about the future. When he thinks about it, these negative appraisals often lead him back into vivid recollections of the event, further fueling his distress. His attempts to cope with these overwhelming feelings include imagining getting revenge on those responsible for the assault. This fantasy provides a temporary release from the emotional pain but reinforces the cycle by keeping the memories and triggers active. The more he thinks about exacting revenge, the more vividly he remembers the traumatic event. Keenan’s sense of being constantly on guard has permeated every aspect of his life. Even inside his own home, he feels as though danger could emerge at any moment. This heightened state of alertness often results in false alarms, where he reacts to benign situations as if they were threats. These reactions further intensify his hypervigilance and make it difficult for him to relax or feel safe. Over time, Keenan’s work has been affected by these symptoms. He finds himself distracted and anxious at the restaurant, particularly when there are sudden movements among the kitchen staff. The constant need to be on guard makes it hard for him to focus on his tasks, leading to mistakes that could compromise both the quality of his dishes and his job security. What finally brought Keenan to seek help was a combination of these occupational challenges and an increasing sense of isolation. He realized he couldn’t continue living in this state of perpetual fear and distress. While he hopes for relief from the constant flashbacks and triggers, what he most fears is never feeling safe again or being able to move past the trauma that has defined his recent life. Keenan’s journey towards recovery begins with acknowledging these complex interconnections between his triggers, maladaptive strategies, heightened threat perception, intrusive memories, and negative appraisals. Through therapy, he aims to find a path toward healing and reclaiming control over his life.
